messages:
jack_support: Customer reported streaming responses cut off after ~25-40s. They see first few tokens, then connection resets. Happens only when requests go via Cloudflare + our nginx ingress in front of the origin. Direct to origin (no CF) seems stable. They call our /v1/stream endpoint with bearer token that rotates every 5m. Also saw a spike in billing events: duplicate sessions. Repro steps and pcap attached to the ticket.
maya: thanks — can you paste a minimal curl repro? also need request id and client region. any 502/504s on the path?
jack_support: curl we asked them to run: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.example.com/v1/stream?model=small"``` they said tcp stream shows FIN from Cloudflare after ~30s. HTTP shows 200 then silence. No explicit 502 from CF.
samir: my hunch: buffering or idle timeout upstream. CF + ALB/nginx can all suppress flushes. Check nginx `proxy_buffering` and `proxy_http_version 1.1` + `proxy_set_header Connection ""` for SSE. Also ALB idle timeout default 60s but weird interactions can cause midstream half-close.
alex: another vector: token rotation. If client reuses an old token and our backend returns 401 mid-stream (rare), CF might close without propagating message. But customer says direct->origin works, so more likely buffering. Can we ask them to run `curl --no-buffer` to see raw effect? Also try adding `X-Debug-Route: true` header to trace which LB/edge served the request.
maya: quick checklist for customer to try (short): 1) curl --no-buffer + Accept: text/event-stream 2) set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on origin if using nginx (disables FastCGI/proxy buffering) 3) ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and responses flush with `\n\n` between events 4) add small whitespace heartbeat every 15s from server side 5) increase ALB/NLB idle timeout to 120s while we debug
jack_support: forwarded checklist. Customer replied: setting `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on their upstream nginx fixed immediate truncation in our staging tests behind CF. They still see occasional reconnection loops in production. Provided pcap showing Cloudflare sending RST to client after origin stops sending for 30s.
samir: that matches proxy idle detection. Cloudflare has proxy_read_timeout and edge inactivity heuristics. If origin goes silent for >30s, CF may terminate. Heartbeats are the most robust workaround. Also check if Cloudflare's "maximum duration of origin connections" setting applies.
ops-bot: Created support incident SI-2026-482 with priority P2. Linked ticket and attached pcap + curl logs.
alex: next steps from our side: 1) add server-side guidance to docs for SSE + CF/nginx/ALB combos (clear list of headers and flush behavior) 2) add a diagnostic endpoint on the API that emits a heartbeat every 10s for repro 3) correlate billing duplicate sessions — maybe client retries on perceived disconnect and token rotation leads to new session creation; that may be inflating billing events.
maya: note for docs snippet to recommend: ```proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on; add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;``` plus server must call `fflush` / `flush` after writes.
jack_support: customer accepted heartbeat + proxy_buffering off workaround while they coordinate with CF support to raise edge timeout. They asked if Redwood can detect and emit a warning when a stream has been silent >20s so clients know to retry gracefully instead of hammering token rotations.
samir: we can add a metric/alert: stream_silence_duration and an API telemetry flag to mark silent streams. Low-effort: add logging when write latency > 15s between flushes. I'll open an infra ticket.
ops-bot: Created internal task INF-807 for silent-stream detection.
alex: summarizing resolution: immediate workaround = disable proxy_buffering on origin/nginx + enable periodic whitespace heartbeat (<=15s). Long term = docs + stream silence telemetry + guidance for CF/ALB idle timeouts. Marking this thread for handoff to docs + infra.
jack_support: thanks all — customer will monitor after CF support adjusts edge timeout and we've deployed heartbeat. Will reopen if any regressions. :thumbsup:
